scope: Website copy for what public v1.34.0 shipped (October 14, 2026): Kagi and a custom search address (any search engine whose address takes the search words, such as SearXNG) in Settings → General → Search engine. Also the Quiet Tabs page's Island figure, its caption, its accessible name and its share-card description (October 15, 2026), redrawn to the dimmed rows v1.34.0 actually shows. Every evidence path is at the immutable publicRelease tag. The retired four-engine wording is recorded as supersededClaims in docs/website-features-bento-claims-v1.30.json; the retired quiet-dot figure wording is recorded as supersededClaims here. Since October 15, 2026 it also records the memory figures from the benchmark re-run on public v1.34.0 (bench/memory/results/memory-2026-10-15T06-03-46-052Z.md), which replaced the 9 August 2026 run with Blanc 1.1.0.
prohibitedClaims: search keywords or shortcuts, or several saved custom search engines
OpenSearch auto-discovery, or importing search engines from other browsers
live search suggestions from a custom search engine
Kagi working without a Kagi account, or sharing its sign-in with private tabs
plain http:// custom search addresses on the open internet
quiet tabs drawn differently on the resting Island's tab dots, or marked by a glyph or text label in the tab list or vertical rail
Blanc using less memory than Brave, or Brave merely "coming closest", in the October 15, 2026 run
Blanc with its blocker off using less memory than Chrome: the ranges overlap (5.4–5.6 GiB against 5.4–6.5 GiB)
memory figures for Windows, Linux, or any machine other than the one measured

search.qualification: Public desktop v1.34.0. Settings → General → Search engine offers DuckDuckGo, Google, Bing, Brave Search, Kagi and Custom…. A custom address has exactly one %s where the words go, after the host and port; it uses https://, or http:// only for this computer or the local network, and syncs with the other settings when Profile Sync is on. Kagi needs a Kagi account and private tabs don't share its sign-in. Kagi shows live suggestions; a custom engine shows none. Search suggestions can be turned off in Settings.

quietTabsFigure.qualification: Public desktop v1.34.0. A quiet tab's row dims as one unit to half strength in the expanded Island (.island-row.quiet) and in the vertical tab rail (.vertical-tab-row.quiet); hover or keyboard focus restores it, and its accessible name says quiet. Those rows carry no glyph or text marker, and the resting Island's tab dots, the Quick Switcher and the start page carry no quiet treatment. Quiet tabs keep their place in the tab order. Eligible inactive background tabs release renderer memory and reload when opened; this is not a CPU, battery or exact-resumption promise. The at-rest list shows ungrouped tabs as plain rows, the current tab's title in bold with its close button showing, under an address field holding the current tab's address. The figure is website markup with sample sites and favicons, not captured app footage.

memory.qualification: Public desktop v1.34.0, measured October 15, 2026 by the owner with the harness above on one Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 27.2, 8 GiB RAM): six ad-heavy sites (five news sites and Speedtest), fresh profiles, no extensions, three repetitions, median of phys_footprint summed across each browser’s process tree. The committed run is bench/memory/results/memory-2026-10-15T06-03-46-052Z.{json,md}; test/unit/public-truth.test.js recomputes the published medians from it. Brave, which also blocks by default, used 1.5 GiB against Blanc’s 1.7 GiB; Blanc with its blocker off used 5.4 GiB against Chrome’s 5.7 GiB, with overlapping ranges.

claims.exactWording: Brave is a useful comparison because it also blocks by default; in that run it used a little less memory than Blanc. The run also included Blanc with blocking disabled, which used about as much as Chrome. These results describe those browser versions and workloads on that machine; they are not Windows or Linux results, or a promise that Blanc will always use less memory.
